verses.1: And David’s days came to an end. He commanded his son Solomon to do as he had commanded him.
verses.2: I go along the paths of all the earth. You will be strengthened, and you will become a man.
verses.3: And you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways and to observe His laws, decrees, and commands as written in Moses’ Torah. This will help you understand everything that you must do, and everything that you must say there.
verses.4: So that the LORD may carry out His words, which He said: “If your children keep walking in obedience before Me, with all their hearts and souls, then no one will be king over you from among the people of Israel.”
verses.5: And you also knew what Yoab son of Zeruya did to me. He did the same things to the two priests of Israel: Abner son of Nor and Amasa son of Itar. He killed them, and he poured their blood into sacrifices during the festival days. He also used their blood as ointment for his clothes and shoes.
verses.6: And you did as you were wise; you did not let his return be in vain.
verses.7: And my iron wings will show mercy. They will be among your offerings, for they have come to me in my exile, from before your brother Abishalom.
verses.8: And behold, with you is Shimei son of Gera, my right-hand man. He cursed me harshly on the day I left my camp. He came down to the valley and said to me, “If you tell me the truth, then I will forgive you.”
verses.9: And now, do not wash him away, for you are a wise man. You know what you will do to him. You will bring his punishment upon him through bloodshed.
verses.10: David was buried with his ancestors in the city of David.
verses.11: And in the days when David ruled over Israel, he ruled for forty years. In Jerusalem, he ruled for thirty-three years.
verses.12: And Solomon sat on the throne of his father David. Thus, he became king.
verses.13: And Adoniyahu, son of Haggith, went to the daughter of Sephah. She said, “Shalom, come here.” He replied, “Shalom.”
verses.14: And he said to me, “Speak to me.” And I said, “Speak.”
verses.15: And he said, “You know that I had a queen. All of Israel turned their faces towards me as kings. The queen became my sister, for she came from Jehovah.”
verses.16: And now, I have one question for you. Do not turn away from me with a sad face. Instead, say to him, “Speak.”
verses.17: And he said to Shlomo, the king: “Do not turn away from me. Instead, give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife.”
verses.18: And the daughter of seven said, “Good, I will speak to you about the king.”
verses.19: And the daughter of seven went to King Solomon to speak with him about Adonijah. The king got up to receive her. He bowed down to her, sat down on his throne, and placed a stool in front of the queen mother. She then sat to his right.
verses.20: And one little girl said to her, “I ask you, do not turn your face away from me.” Then the king said to her, “I ask my mother, for I will not turn my face away from you.”
verses.21: And he said, “Give Abishag the Shunamite to your brother Adonai as a wife.”
verses.22: And King Solomon said to his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunamite for Adonija? I want to ask him myself, because he is my brother, and also the priest Abiathar and Joab son of Zeruya.”
verses.23: And King Solomon said, “May God do this for me.” He said this because in his heart he believed that Adonai would fulfill His word.
verses.24: And now, may the Lord live! He who prepared me and placed me on the throne of David, my father. He also made preparations for me in that house, just as He said would happen. Today, Adonai will die.
verses.25: And King Solomon sent Benyahu, son of Jehoiada, to do this. But he was killed by him.
verses.26: And the priest said to the king, “Ask for your wages for your servants. For one of your men has died. And on this day, I will not pay you your wages, since you carried the Ark of God before David, my father. And you also fasted in all the ways in which my father did.”
verses.27: And Solomon drove Abiyatar away from his position as priest of Yahweh, so that he could carry out the words of Yahweh that were spoken regarding the house of Eli.
verses.28: And hearing came to Joab. But Joab did not follow Adonijah or Abishalom. Instead, Joab went to the temple of God. There, he strengthened his eyes with the help of divine power.
verses.29: And he reported to King Solomon that Joab had gone to the Temple of God. Then Solomon sent Benyahu, son of Jehoiada, with a message: “Kill him.”
verses.30: And Benyaahu went to the temple of Jehovah. He said to him, “As the king said, ‘Get out!’” But he replied, “Not here.” Then Benyaahu took the king’s words back. He said, “This is what Yoab said, and this is what I will do.”
verses.31: And the king said to him, “Do as he has said. Punish him and bury him. Also, remove the bloodstains from his clothes, which have been spilled on his body and on my father’s house.”
verses.32: And Jehovah restored his soul to its rightful place. He had caused harm to two righteous and good people. David, my father, did not know about Abner, the commander of the Israelite army, nor about Amasa, the commander of the Jewish army.
verses.33: And their memory shall be preserved forever in the head of Joab and in the head of his descendants. It will be a source of peace for David and his descendants, as well as for his house and throne. Peace will reign forever with Jehovah.
verses.34: And Benyahu, son of Yehoyada, was killed. He died and was buried in his house in the desert.
verses.35: And the king gave his son, Yehoyada, to be under his command over the army. He also gave the priest Zadok to be under Abiyatar’s command.
verses.36: And the king sent for Shemira and said to him, “Go into the house in Jerusalem. You shall sit there, and you shall not leave that place again.”
verses.37: And it shall be that on the day you leave and cross the river Kedron, you will know that your blood will be shed on your head.
verses.38: And Shimei said to the king, “It is good advice that you have given. Your servant will do as you say.” Then Shimei stayed in Jerusalem for many days.
verses.39: After three years, two servants went to Shem, to the house of Ahishah, king of Gath. They told Shem, “Look, your servants are in Gath.”
verses.40: And Shimei got up, broke his spear, and went to Achish to ask for his servants. Shimei brought his servants back from Gath.
verses.41: And he told Shlomo that Shemaiah had gone from Jerusalem and returned.
verses.42: And the king sent for Shimei and said to him, “May God bless you! I promise you that on the day you leave, I will know that you will die.” And he replied, “That’s a good thing to hear.”
verses.43: And why did you not keep the commands of Jehovah, and the laws I commanded you?
verses.44: And the king said to Shimei, “You know all the evil that you did to David, my father. Now, Jehovah has restored your evil back to you.”
verses.45: And King Solomon, who is blessed and worthy of David’s honor, will be willing to serve before Jehovah forever.
verses.46: The king commanded Benjamin, son of Jehoiada, to go out and fight against them. But he was killed in battle. Then the kingdom fell into the hands of Solomon.
